correctness.rationale: Every selected isolated chord partitions the remaining endpoints into independent uniform matchings; exact event probability p_{n,r}, conditional crossings and oriented-chord counting give the finite expression. Strict negativity holds for n>=2. Pairing the r=0,n-1 and r=1,n-2 terms with a geometric ratio tail bound yields the two sharp asymptotics. The standalone exact-rational verifier independently exhausts all 146599 matchings through n=7 (including boundary n=1 checked only computationally) and reproduces mixed moments. Finite checks are corroboration, not a replacement for the analytic argument.

value.rationale: Isolated chords are degree-zero vertices and crossing pairs are edges of a natural random circle graph. The exact covariance quantifies the dependence of local disconnection on global intersection density. More strikingly, non-simple isolated chords have expectation 1/(2n)+O(n^-2) and tend to zero in probability, yet their covariance with the growing edge statistic converges to -1/3. This naturally motivated nonuniform-integrability correction changes the second-order constant of the all-isolates covariance and is not a routine reindexing of simple-chord moments.
